mainTopic: Helping animals and people on שבת and יום טוב: moving animals without carrying, צער בעלי חיים, assisting births, and breaking שבת for a יולדת
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: spoiled meat and exposed water may be moved on שבת because animals can use them, though רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says exposed water should not be kept at all because of danger. A new משנה then teaches how to help chicks, a runaway hen, calves, foals and a child move on שבת without carrying them. The גמרא brings רב's ruling that one may put cushions under an animal stuck in a water channel when it cannot be fed in place, because צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law that overrides the rabbinic rule of מבטל כלי מהיכנו. Next it explains that a hen may only be pushed, not helped to walk, because it lifts itself off the ground, and it uses this to settle an apparent contradiction in a ברייתא. A second משנה permits only assisting an animal giving birth on יום טוב, while for a woman in labor one may break שבת fully. The גמרא defines this 'assisting' and explains how to help a kosher mother animal accept her newborn. It then lists what may be done for a יולדת: lighting a lamp, even for a blind woman, and bringing oil in the least usual way possible. The amud ends with שמואל's rule that while the womb is open, שבת is broken for her whether or not she asks. His rule for after the womb closes continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Swollen meat and exposed water may be moved because animals can use them
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: spoiled meat and exposed water are not מוקצה, because animals can still use them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Swollen meat may be moved because it is food for wild animals. Exposed water may be moved because it is fit for a cat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that lists things people no longer want but that may still be moved on שבת. It explains why each item is not מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that has started to rot is not fit for people, but wild animals will eat it, so it still has a use. Water left uncovered might have snake venom in it, so people should not drink it. A cat can still drink it, so it is not totally useless.

keyTerms.meaning: Swollen meat that has started to rot
Water left uncovered, possibly poisoned by a snake

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new topic. It is the tail end of a ברייתא that began earlier on the דף, about which items are or are not מוקצה.

phrases.english: Swollen meat —
because it is food for wild animals;
phrases.notes: It may be moved because it still has a use.

phrases.english: exposed water —
phrases.notes: A snake may have drunk from it and left venom.

phrases.english: because it is fit for a cat.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּשָׂר תָּפוּחַ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכָל לְחַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא earlier about items that are not מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item unfit for people is still not מוקצה if it is fit for animals, such as rotting meat for wild animals or exposed water for a cat.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: exposed water should not be kept at all
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says exposed water may not be kept, because of the danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: one may not keep exposed water at all, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds his own view about the exposed water from the previous step. He says it should not be kept at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion treated exposed water as something useful for a cat, so it may be moved. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל looks at it differently: since a person might drink it by mistake, it must not be kept around at all. His worry is about safety, not about מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives his own view here
To keep them, to leave them around

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common principle: concern for danger to life (סכנה) is taken very seriously and can change how we treat an item.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
it is forbidden to keep them at all
phrases.notes: Refers to the exposed water.

phrases.english: because of the danger.
phrases.notes: Someone might drink it by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view about the exposed water in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exposed water may not be kept at all because of the danger that someone will drink it.

steps.title: The משנה: helping chicks and a runaway hen without carrying them
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה permits overturning a basket so chicks can climb, and pushing a runaway hen back inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may turn a basket upside down in front of chicks so they can climb up and down. A hen that ran away may be pushed until it goes back in.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches ways to help animals on שבת without picking them up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals are מוקצה, so one may not carry them. Instead, one may turn a basket over so the chicks climb up and down by themselves. One may also push a runaway hen back home, since pushing is not the same as lifting it.

keyTerms.meaning: One turns the basket upside down

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not allow picking up the chicks or the hen. It only allows helping them move on their own.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may overturn the basket in front of the chicks
so that they can climb up and climb down.
A hen that ran away —
one may push it until it goes back in.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כּוֹפִין אֶת הַסַּל לִפְנֵי הָאֶפְרוֹחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may help birds move on שבת, by overturning a basket or pushing, but may not carry them.

steps.title: The משנה: helping calves, foals and a child walk
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits supporting calves and foals as they walk, and a mother may help her son walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may help calves and foals walk. A woman may help her son walk.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with more cases of helping on שבת. This time it is walking: young animals and a small child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדדין means holding the animal or child by the sides so it can walk. The animal or child is still walking on its own feet, so this is not counted as carrying. This sets up רבי יהודה's limit in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One helps them walk, holding them up as they step

phrases.english: One may help calves and foals walk.
A woman may help her son walk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases of helping without carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may support calves, foals and a child while they walk on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only if the child really takes steps
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the permission to a child who lifts one foot and puts down the other. If the child drags his feet, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When is this allowed? When the child lifts one foot and puts down the other. But if he drags his feet, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a limit to the rule about a mother helping her son walk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the child really steps on his own, he is walking and the mother is only helping. If he just drags his feet, the mother is really carrying him. In a public area (רשות הרבים) that would be forbidden carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds a limit to the rule
Lifts one foot and puts down one foot, real steps

steps.whatToRemember: Helping a child walk is fine only if the child is really walking. If you are basically holding him up and his feet drag, it counts as carrying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When is this?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל אַחַת וּמַנִּיחַ אַחַת,
phrases.english: When he lifts one foot and puts down one foot,
but if he was dragging his feet, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Then it is like carrying him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mother may help her son walk only when he takes real steps. If he drags his feet, it is forbidden.

steps.title: רב: cushions may be placed under an animal that fell into a water channel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב's rule: for an animal that fell into a water channel, one may put cushions and blankets under it so it can climb out.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If an animal fell into a water channel, one brings pillows and blankets and puts them under it. If it climbs out, it climbs out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a rule from רב about saving an animal on שבת. One may not lift it out, but one may help it climb out by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the משנה's idea: help the animal, but don't carry it. Putting cushions in the water ruins them for normal use, which is usually a problem on שבת. The concern for the animal's suffering (צער בעלי חיים) allows it, as the גמרא explains in Steps 9–10.

keyTerms.meaning: If it climbs out, it climbs out

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is a main source for the idea that צער בעלי חיים can allow things that are normally forbidden by the רבנן on שבת.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
An animal that fell into a water channel —
one brings pillows and blankets
and places them beneath it,
and if it climbs out, it climbs out.
phrases.notes: The person does not lift it. It climbs out by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנָּפְלָה לְאַמַּת הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens with a rule that matches the משנה's theme of helping animals without carrying them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an animal that fell into a water channel, one may place pillows and blankets under it so it can climb out by itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to allow only feeding, not cushions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says to feed the trapped animal where it is. This suggests that feeding is allowed but cushions and blankets are not, which contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: An animal that fell into a water channel: one gives it food where it is, so that it will not die. Food, yes; cushions and blankets, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's rule from Step 6 by quoting a ברייתא that only mentions feeding the trapped animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists one way to help the animal: bring it food (פרנסה) where it is. The גמרא reads this precisely. If only food is mentioned, then cushions and blankets must be forbidden, and that clashes with רב's permission.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
Yes ... no (the pattern of a precise inference)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
An animal that fell into a water channel —
one gives it food in its place
phrases.notes: He feeds it where it is and does not take it out.

phrases.english: so that it will not die.
Food — yes,
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא starts drawing a conclusion from the wording.

phrases.english: cushions and blankets — no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to place cushions and blankets under the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא mentions only food, which implies that cushions and blankets are forbidden.

steps.title: Food when possible, cushions when not
steps.stepSummary: The two sources deal with different situations. The ברייתא speaks where feeding is possible. רב speaks where it is not, and then cushions are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where feeding is possible; that one is where feeding is not possible. If feeding is possible, yes, feed it. If not, he brings cushions and blankets and places them under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the ברייתא and רב are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding the animal in place is the first choice. When that can't be done, for example because the animal would drown or can't be reached, רב's cushions become allowed. So the two sources set an order of options and do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the sources speak of different cases)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that you choose the milder method first, and only if that fails do you move to the method that involves more שבת concerns.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
this one — where feeding is possible,
phrases.notes: This one is the ברייתא.

phrases.english: that one — where feeding is not possible.
phrases.notes: That one is רב's ruling.

phrases.english: If feeding is possible — yes (he feeds it),
and if not — he brings cushions and blankets
and places them beneath it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (אוקימתא of two situations)
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks where feeding works. רב permits cushions where feeding is not possible.

steps.title: Doesn't using the cushions take them out of use?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: by putting the cushions in the water under the animal, isn't he making a usable item unavailable for use on שבת (מבטל כלי מהיכנו)?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is negating a vessel's readiness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רב's ruling: placing cushions under the animal seems to break a different שבת rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the cushions are under the animal, they can't be moved or used for the rest of שבת, because the animal is מוקצה and is lying on them. Taking an item out of its usable state on שבת is called מבטל כלי מהיכנו, and it resembles breaking something down.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a usable item unusable on שבת

phrases.english: But he is negating a vessel's readiness!
phrases.notes: The cushions are now stuck in a state where they cannot be used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב's ruling, now that it is limited to cases where feeding is impossible
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing cushions and blankets under the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes the cushions unusable for the rest of שבת, which should be forbidden.

steps.title: The Torah law of animal suffering overrides a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that מבטל כלי מהיכנו is only rabbinic, while צער בעלי חיים is a Torah prohibition. A Torah law pushes aside a rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that negating a vessel's readiness is rabbinic, and causing pain to animals is a Torah law, and the Torah law comes and pushes aside the rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule about making items unusable is only rabbinic, so preventing the animal's suffering, which is a Torah obligation, wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a clash between two rules. מבטל כלי מהיכנו is דרבנן, and צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא. When the two collide, the stronger Torah law overrides the rabbinic one, so the cushions are permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this סוגיא, צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law, and it overrides the rabbinic rule of מבטל כלי מהיכנו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the view that צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא, a principle quoted widely in הלכה.

phrases.english: He holds: negating a vessel's readiness is rabbinic,
causing pain to animals is a Torah law,
and the Torah law comes and overrides the rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking of laws: a Torah law overrides a rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the cushions unusable should forbid using them.
steps.terutzMaskana: That prohibition is only rabbinic and gives way to the Torah law of צער בעלי חיים.

steps.title: From the משנה: push a hen, but don't help it walk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a runaway hen and reads it precisely: pushing it back is allowed, but helping it walk is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hen that ran away, etc. Pushing, yes; helping it walk, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה (Step 3) and draws an inference from it. This sets up the next step, which shows the inference was already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'push' (דוחין) for the hen, not 'help walk' (מדדין) as it does for calves. The גמרא concludes that helping a hen walk is forbidden. The reason comes a few steps later, from אביי in Step 14: a hen lifts itself off the ground, so 'helping' it becomes carrying it.

keyTerms.meaning: We help it walk by supporting it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two verbs. Pushing a hen from behind is allowed. Holding it up as it walks (מדדין) is forbidden for a hen, even though it is allowed for calves and foals.

phrases.english: A hen that ran away, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: Pushing — yes; helping it walk — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the animal in the water to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A runaway hen may be pushed but may not be helped to walk.

steps.title: A ברייתא already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this inference was already taught in a ברייתא: animals and birds may be helped to walk in a courtyard, but not a hen.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this, as the Rabbis taught: One may help a domestic animal, a wild animal, and a bird walk in the courtyard, but not a hen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the inference from Step 11 by showing a ברייתא that states it openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows supporting most creatures as they walk, but makes an explicit exception for hens. This confirms that the משנה's word 'push' was chosen on purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: You may help animals and birds walk on שבת in a courtyard, except a hen, which may only be pushed.

phrases.english: We already learned this,
as the Rabbis taught:
One may help a domestic animal, a wild animal, and a bird walk in the courtyard,
but not the hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference of Step 11
steps.raayaObject: The inference that a hen may not be helped to walk
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: מדדין בהמה חיה ועוף בחצר אבל לא את התרנגולת

steps.title: Why may one not help a hen walk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that a hen is excluded from the permission to help animals walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hen: what is the reason that one may not help it walk?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא we just saw allowed helping animals and birds walk in a חצר, but not a hen. The גמרא now asks why the hen is different, and sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only know the rule: a hen is excluded. This question asks for the reason behind it. Other birds may be helped, so something about a hen in particular must change the law.

phrases.english: A hen, what is the reason that [one may] not [help it walk]?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the ברייתא in Step 12, which excluded a hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the hen exception taught in the ברייתא of Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a hen, unlike other fowl, may not be helped to walk on שבת.

steps.title: A hen lifts itself off the ground
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a hen raises itself up, so helping it walk amounts to carrying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because it lifts itself up.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. When you try to help a hen walk, it pulls its feet off the ground, so you end up holding its whole weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping an animal walk is allowed because the animal still carries itself and you only guide it. A hen lifts its legs, so you are really carrying it, and carrying an animal on שבת is not allowed. The hen is still a bird like the others. Its behavior simply turns 'helping' into 'carrying.'

keyTerms.meaning: It lifts itself up (draws its legs off the ground)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Because it lifts itself up [off the ground].
phrases.notes: As a result, the person ends up carrying the hen completely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hen lifts its feet off the ground, so 'helping it walk' really becomes carrying it, which is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the line between permitted 'helping' and forbidden 'carrying' depends on whether the animal still bears its own weight.

steps.title: Two ברייתות about moving animals in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes one ברייתא allowing helping animals walk in a חצר, and a second ברייתא forbidding lifting them but allowing pushing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא taught: One may help a domestic animal, a wild animal, and a bird walk in a חצר, but not in רשות הרבים. A woman may help her son walk in רשות הרבים, and needless to say in a חצר. Another ברייתא taught: One may not lift a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird in a חצר, but one may push them so they will go in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות on the topic of moving animals on שבת. This is a setup: the next step will point out a problem inside the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא gives three levels. Animals may be helped in a חצר, not in רשות הרבים, and a child may be helped even in רשות הרבים. The second ברייתא sets two levels: lifting is forbidden and pushing is allowed. Keep in mind exactly what each one says, because the next step depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting (uprooting) an animal off the ground

steps.confusionAlert: There are three different actions here. עוקרין means lifting it fully, and that is forbidden. מדדין means holding it while it walks on its own feet. דוחין means only pushing it from behind. Keep the three apart, or the next step will not make sense.

phrases.english: One [ברייתא] taught:
One may help a domestic animal, a wild animal, and a bird walk in the courtyard,
but not in the public domain.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאִשָּׁה מְדַדָּה אֶת בְּנָהּ בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: And a woman may help her son walk in the public domain,
and needless to say in the courtyard.
And another [ברייתא] taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹקְרִין בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה וָעוֹף בֶּחָצֵר,
phrases.english: One may not lift a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird in the courtyard,
but one may push them so that they will enter.
phrases.notes: Pushing is allowed, and this sets up the question of whether helping them walk is also allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings more ברייתות on the subject of moving animals, preparing an internal difficulty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Helping animals walk is allowed in a חצר but not in רשות הרבים. Lifting them is forbidden, and pushing them is allowed.

steps.title: The second ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The first clause implies that helping an animal walk is allowed, while the last clause implies it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said 'one may not lift,' which implies that helping them walk is allowed. Then you said 'pushing, yes,' which implies that helping them walk is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the second ברייתא contradicts itself depending on which clause you read precisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only lifting is forbidden, then the next level down, helping it walk, should be allowed. But if only pushing is allowed, then the level just above pushing, helping it walk, should be forbidden. Helping it walk sits in the middle, and each clause points it in a different direction.

keyTerms.meaning: This [source] itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said 'one may not lift,'
but helping walk, we do help walk.
Then you said:
Pushing, yes; helping walk, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second ברייתא quoted in Step 15 by showing that its two clauses imply opposite rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second ברייתא (אין עוקרין, אבל דוחין).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From the רישא, helping an animal walk is permitted, since only lifting is forbidden. From the סיפא, helping it walk is forbidden, since only pushing is permitted. This is an internal contradiction.

steps.title: The last clause is about a hen
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the סיפא, which allows only pushing, refers specifically to a hen.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In the last clause we have come to a hen.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the two halves of the ברייתא speak about different creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא is about animals and birds in general, and they may be helped to walk. The סיפא is about a hen, which may only be pushed, because it lifts itself up (Step 14). So both inferences are correct, each for its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a source
We have come to (the clause now speaks about)

steps.whatToRemember: Most animals and birds may be helped to walk in a חצר on שבת. A hen may only be pushed, because it lifts itself, so helping it turns into carrying it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the last clause, we have come to a hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the רישא and the סיפא refer to different subjects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses of the ברייתא refer to the same animals, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא covers animals and birds in general, which may be helped to walk. The סיפא covers a hen, which may only be pushed.

steps.title: How to hold a hen during slaughter
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that a person slaughtering a hen should press its legs to the ground or lift it fully, so that it does not tear out the סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone who slaughters a hen should press its legs into the ground, or else lift it fully into the air. Otherwise it might plant its claws in the ground, jerk, and tear out the סימנים.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is hens, the גמרא brings a related practical teaching from אביי about שחיטה. It is a side point and not part of the שבת discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a hen's claws touch the ground during שחיטה, it can push off and jerk its body. That jerk can rip the windpipe and food pipe out of place, which is called עיקור, and the שחיטה would then be invalid. Either pinning the legs down or holding the hen completely in the air prevents this.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe and food pipe that must be cut in שחיטה
Tears out (dislodges); this ruins the שחיטה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for שחיטה. Torn-out סימנים would make the bird a נבלה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who slaughters a hen
should press its legs into the ground,
or alternatively lift it up completely,
since perhaps it will place its claws on the ground
and tear out the סימנים.
phrases.notes: The windpipe and food pipe are torn out of place, which invalidates the שחיטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּשָׁחֵיט תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An associative teaching. Since hens were just discussed, the גמרא adds another teaching of אביי about hens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When slaughtering a hen, either pin its legs to the ground or hold it fully in the air, so it cannot push off with its claws and tear out the סימנים.

steps.title: The משנה: Birthing an Animal versus a Woman
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids fully delivering an animal on יום טוב but allows assisting it. It allows full help for a woman giving birth on שבת, including breaking שבת for her. It also allows tying the umbilical cord (רבי יוסי allows even cutting it) and all the needs of a מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not deliver an animal on יום טוב, but one may assist it. One may deliver a woman's baby on שבת, call a midwife for her from place to place, and break שבת for her. One may also tie the umbilical cord. רבי יוסי says: one may even cut it. And all the needs of a מילה may be done on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out the rules for helping with births on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. For an animal, there is no danger to human life, so only light 'assisting' is allowed, and only on יום טוב. For a woman, her life may be in danger, so we break שבת fully for her, even by calling a midwife from far away.

keyTerms.meaning: Fully delivering a baby or newborn animal
Assisting, giving light help without doing the full delivery
Everything needed to perform a ברית מילה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two verbs. מילדין means doing the actual delivery, while מסעדין means only helping along. The animal gets only מסעדין, and only on יום טוב. The woman gets full מילדין, even on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the rule that we break שבת for a woman in labor.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מְיַלְּדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may not deliver an animal on a Festival,
but one may assist.
And one may deliver a woman on Shabbat,
and call a midwife for her from place to place,
and desecrate Shabbat for her,
and tie the umbilical cord.
Rabbi Yosei says: one may even cut it.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי goes further than the תנא קמא, who allows only tying.

phrases.english: And all the needs of circumcision are done on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מְיַלְּדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of moving animals and slaughtering a hen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animal: no full delivery on יום טוב, only assisting. Woman: full delivery and breaking שבת are allowed. Tying the cord is allowed (רבי יוסי: even cutting). All needs of מילה are allowed.

steps.title: What Does 'Assisting' an Animal Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how one may assist an animal giving birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: How does one assist?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of help the משנה means by 'assisting.' This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה drew a line between delivering (forbidden) and assisting (allowed), but it never said what assisting looks like. The גמרא wants that line defined.

phrases.english: GEMARA: How does one assist?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a word in the משנה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: Catching the Newborn
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says assisting means holding the newborn so it does not fall to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: One holds the newborn so that it does not fall to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first answer: assisting means catching the newborn as it comes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, assisting happens only after the birth is already taking place. One does nothing to push the birth along, but only keeps the newborn from getting hurt.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One holds the newborn
so that it does not fall to the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Assisting means catching the newborn so it does not fall.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Pressing to Help It Come Out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says assisting means pressing on the flesh so the newborn comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: One presses on the flesh so that the newborn comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different answer. He says assisting includes pressing on the mother so the baby animal comes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן allows more active help, which actually moves the birth forward. In his view, only pulling the newborn out counts as forbidden 'delivering.'

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh (of the mother animal, around the womb)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
One presses on the flesh
so that the newborn comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה's answer in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Assisting includes pressing on the mother to help the newborn come out.

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches רב יהודה: one catches the newborn, blows into its nose, and puts the teat into its mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב יהודה: How does one assist? One holds the newborn so it does not fall to the ground, blows into its nose, and puts the teat into its mouth so it will nurse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines assisting the same way רב יהודה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only care given to the newborn after it emerges, and it says nothing about pressing to push it out. This supports רב יהודה over רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with him

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda:
How does one assist?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹחֲזִין אֶת הַוָּלָד שֶׁלֹּא יִפּוֹל לָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: One holds the newborn so that it does not fall to the ground,
and blows into its nose,
phrases.notes: This clears the mucus so the newborn can breathe.

phrases.english: and puts the teat into its mouth
so that it will nurse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב יהודה in the dispute of steps 21 and 22.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that defines מסעדין as holding, blowing into the nose, and helping the newborn nurse
steps.whatToRemember: מסעדין means caring for the newborn as it comes out: catching it, clearing its nose, and helping it nurse. A ברייתא supports this view of רב יהודה.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Helping a Kosher Mother Pity Its Young
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that on יום טוב they used to show mercy to kosher animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: We used to show mercy to a kosher animal on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He adds another kind of help: showing mercy to a kosher animal on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes beyond the birth itself. It deals with a mother animal that will not accept its newborn. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they would help even in that situation, but he limits it to a kosher animal.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
We used to show mercy to a kosher animal
on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and adds a new kind of help.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may act to make a kosher mother animal take pity on its newborn.

steps.title: How Was This Mercy Shown?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was actually done to show mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what action רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant. This sets up אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Showing mercy' is vague. The גמרא wants the specific action that is permitted on יום טוב.

phrases.english: How does one do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method of making the mother animal pity its newborn.

steps.title: אביי: Salt and Afterbirth Fluid
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains two methods. One puts a lump of salt in the womb so the mother remembers her pain and pities the newborn. One also sprinkles afterbirth fluid on the newborn so the mother smells it and pities it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: One brings a lump of salt and places it in her womb, so she remembers her pain and has pity on the newborn. And one sprinkles the fluid of the afterbirth on the newborn, so she smells its scent and has pity on it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives two practical ways to get a mother animal to accept its newborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salt causes pain, which reminds the mother of the pain of giving birth, so she connects to the newborn. The afterbirth fluid gives the newborn her own familiar scent, so she recognizes it as hers.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One brings a lump of salt
and places it in her womb,
so that she remembers her pain and has pity on it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמְזַלְּפִין מֵי שִׁלְיָא עַל גַּבֵּי וָלָד,
phrases.english: And one sprinkles afterbirth fluid on the newborn,
so that she smells its scent and has pity on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מֵבִיא בּוּל שֶׁל מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Put salt in the womb, and sprinkle afterbirth fluid on the newborn.

steps.title: Only for a Kosher Animal
steps.stepSummary: These methods are allowed only for a kosher animal, not a non-kosher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies specifically to a kosher animal, but not to a non-kosher one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes by stressing that this mercy is allowed only for a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats and confirms the limit in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words, 'בהמה טהורה.' The methods of אביי are permitted on יום טוב for a kosher animal, but not for a non-kosher one.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב one may help a kosher mother animal accept its newborn, using salt and afterbirth fluid. This is not done for a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: And specifically a kosher one,
but a non-kosher one, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit on אביי's methods.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The permission to make the mother animal pity its young applies only to a kosher animal.

steps.title: Why not for a non-kosher animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the mercy methods are allowed only for a kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the methods from the last step (salt and afterbirth fluid) are allowed only for a בהמה טהורה and not a בהמה טמאה. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step drew a line between kosher and non-kosher animals but gave no reason. The גמרא wants to know what makes the non-kosher case different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Asking why the mercy methods do not apply to a non-kosher animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the limit stated in Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the mercy methods are limited to kosher animals.

steps.title: A non-kosher animal's nature makes the methods useless
steps.stepSummary: A non-kosher mother does not reject her young. If she does reject it, she will not take it back. So the methods accomplish nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher animal does not push away its young. And if it does push away its young, it does not bring it close again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a בהמה טמאה behaves differently. Either she never rejects her baby, or once she rejects it, nothing will make her accept it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The methods are allowed on יום טוב only because they actually help. For a non-kosher animal they serve no purpose. Doing them would be pointless effort on יום טוב, so they are not allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The mercy methods on יום טוב are allowed only where they actually work, which means only for a kosher animal.

phrases.english: A non-kosher animal does not push away its young,
and if it does push away its young, it does not bring it close again.
phrases.notes: Either way, the methods would not help.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Non-kosher animals either do not reject their young or never take them back, so the methods are pointless.

steps.title: What does the extra phrase about a woman giving birth add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a woman giving birth. It asks what 'one may desecrate שבת for her' adds beyond what the משנה already listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may help a woman give birth, etc.' After all, the משנה already taught: one may help a woman give birth and call a midwife for her from place to place. So what does 'and one may desecrate שבת for her' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, about a יולדת. It points out that the phrase 'ומחללין עליה את השבת' looks extra and asks what it adds. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already allowed helping with the birth and calling a midwife (חכמה) from another place. A general phrase allowing חילול שבת then seems to repeat what was already said. The גמרא assumes no words are wasted, so the phrase must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: One helps a woman give birth
One may do acts normally forbidden on שבת
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: 'One may help a woman give birth, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: After all, it was already taught:
One may help a woman give birth
and call a midwife for her from place to place,
'and one may desecrate שבת for her'
comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה about a woman giving birth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new case the general phrase 'ומחללין עליה את השבת' adds.

steps.title: It adds lighting a lamp and bringing oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a friend may light a lamp for the יולדת. She may also bring oil: first in her hand, then in her hair, and finally in a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include what the Rabbis taught: if she needs a lamp, her friend lights the lamp for her. If she needs oil, her friend brings her oil in her hand. If what fits in her hand is not enough, she brings it in her hair. If what fits in her hair is not enough, she brings it in a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra phrase includes more needs of the יולדת, as listed in a ברייתא. These are lighting a lamp and carrying oil to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets an order for carrying the oil. The friend first uses an unusual way of carrying (שינוי), such as in her hand or hair. Only if that is not enough does she carry it the normal way, in a vessel. The idea is to break שבת as little as possible while still meeting the woman's needs.
steps.confusionAlert: Bringing the oil is not a free-for-all. The ברייתא lists an order: hand, then hair, then vessel. Each step is used only if the one before is not enough.

phrases.english: To include that which the Rabbis taught:
If she needed a lamp,
her friend lights the lamp for her.
And if she needed oil,
her friend brings her oil in her hand,
phrases.notes: An unusual way of carrying.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ סֹפֵק בַּיָּד — מְבִיאָה בִּשְׂעָרָהּ,
phrases.english: and if the hand is not enough, she brings it in her hair,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ סֹפֵק בִּשְׂעָרָהּ — מְבִיאָה לָהּ בִּכְלִי.
phrases.english: and if the hair is not enough, she brings it for her in a vessel.
phrases.notes: The normal way of carrying, used only as a last resort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 30 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes lighting a lamp and bringing oil, with the oil carried in a set order from least to most normal.

steps.title: Isn't lighting a lamp obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the lamp rule from the ברייתא and asks why it needs to be said, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'If she needed a lamp, her friend lights the lamp for her.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and challenges it as obvious. A woman in labor clearly needs light, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that חילול שבת is allowed for a יולדת. Lighting a lamp so the helpers can see seems like a plain example of that. Saying it outright seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting the previous source again)

phrases.english: The Master said:
If she needed a lamp,
her friend lights the lamp for her.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the ברייתא from Step 31 to challenge its first line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lamp clause of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems self-evident, so stating it appears unnecessary.

steps.title: The rule is needed for a blind woman
steps.stepSummary: The rule teaches that even for a blind יולדת one may light a lamp, because it calms her to know her friend can see and help her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for a blind woman. You might have said: since she cannot see, it is forbidden. So it teaches us that lighting it settles her mind. She thinks: if something is needed, my friend will see it and do it for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a blind woman (סומא). Even though she cannot use the light herself, the lamp may still be lit for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that light is useless to someone who cannot see, so lighting it would be forbidden. The ברייתא teaches that her peace of mind (יתובי דעתא) is itself a good enough reason to break שבת. Knowing her helper can see protects her from dangerous fear.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this case)
Her mind is settled, she is calmed

steps.whatToRemember: A יולדת's peace of mind is a valid reason to break שבת. That is why a lamp is lit even for a blind woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that permission to break שבת for a יולדת covers her emotional state as well as her physical needs, since her fear itself can put her in danger.

phrases.english: It is needed only for a blind woman,
you might have said:
since she cannot see, it is forbidden,
so it teaches us
that her mind is settled by it,
she thinks: if there is anything needed,
my friend will see and do it for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 32 by pointing to a case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to a specific case where it is needed (the blind woman).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a blind woman cannot benefit from the light, lighting a lamp for her would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is allowed, because the light calms her mind by letting her friend see and help.

steps.title: Carrying oil in hair should still be forbidden because of wringing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule about bringing oil for the יולדת in one's hair. It challenges this: the oil will have to be squeezed out of the hair, which is סחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ruling said: 'If she needed oil,' and so on. But this should be forbidden anyway, because of wringing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the oil rule and attacks it. It argues that carrying oil in hair causes a new problem: wringing the hair to get the oil out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of carrying oil in the hair was to make the act of carrying unusual, so it is less of a שבת violation. But the oil soaks into the hair, and getting it out means squeezing. Squeezing liquid out of something is the forbidden act of סחיטה. So the advice seems to swap one problem for another.

keyTerms.meaning: Derive it from / let it be forbidden anyway because of
Wringing or squeezing liquid out of something, a forbidden act on שבת
Et cetera. It signals that the quoted text continues

phrases.english: If she needed oil, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the earlier ruling: she brings the oil in her hair.

phrases.english: Derive that it is forbidden because of wringing!
phrases.notes: The friend would have to squeeze the oil out of her hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the lamp rule (steps 32-33) to the next part of the ברייתא, the oil rule, and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one brings oil for the יולדת in one's hair.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying oil in hair requires squeezing it out later, which is סחיטה. So the method does not avoid a שבת violation.

steps.title: Hair cannot be wrung
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף answer that there is no סחיטה with hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: There is no wringing with hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer to the challenge: squeezing hair is not considered forbidden wringing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair does not soak up liquid the way cloth does. The oil only sits on its surface. So getting the oil off the hair is not the act of סחיטה, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no wringing with hair

phrases.english: It was Rabba and Rav Yosef who both said:
There is no wringing with hair.
phrases.notes: Hair does not absorb liquid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סחיטה challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise. The forbidden act of סחיטה does not apply to hair.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed squeezing oil from hair counts as סחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hair does not absorb liquid, so there is no סחיטה. Carrying oil in hair is fine.

steps.title: The oil is carried in a vessel tied in the hair
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently. Even if hair can be wrung, the oil is carried in a vessel tied in her hair. We change the way we do a שבת action whenever we can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say there is wringing with hair, she brings it in a vessel through her hair. As much as it is possible to change, we change.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, different answer. רב אשי accepts that hair might be wrung, but says the oil never touches the hair. It is in a container tied in the hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil is inside a vessel, so there is no squeezing at all. Why carry the vessel in the hair instead of in the hand? Even when שבת may be broken to save a life, we still do the act in an unusual way when that is possible. This is the principle of שינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say. It means 'even if we accept the opposite view'
Through her hair (tied or carried in her hair)
As much as it is possible to do it differently, we do it differently
Doing an act in an unusual way to lessen the שבת violation

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a basic principle for פיקוח נפש on שבת: when a change in method is possible without harming the patient, we make that change.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רבה and רב יוסף. They say hair cannot be wrung. רב אשי says that even if it can, there is no problem, because the oil is in a vessel.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say there is wringing with hair,
she brings it to her in a vessel through her hair,
phrases.notes: The oil is in a container, so it never soaks into the hair.

phrases.english: for as much as it is possible to change, we change.
phrases.notes: This is why the vessel goes in the hair and not in the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא יֵשׁ סְחִיטָה בְּשֵׂיעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 34, one that works even if רבה and רב יוסף are wrong.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case. 'In her hair' means in a vessel tied in her hair.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the oil was smeared directly on the hair.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oil is in a vessel carried in her hair. There is no squeezing, and the unusual carrying fulfills the rule of making a change where possible.

steps.title: While the womb is open, שבת is desecrated for her no matter what she says
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that as long as the womb is open, we desecrate שבת for the חיה whether or not she says she needs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: A woman giving birth, as long as the womb is open, whether she said 'I need it' or did not say 'I need it,' we desecrate שבת for her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It sets the time period during which the יולדת is automatically treated as being in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the womb is still open, the woman is assumed to be in danger. So we do not wait for her to ask. Her words do not matter, and we desecrate שבת for her either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means the womb, not a grave

steps.confusionAlert: Here קבר means the womb, not a grave. Reading it as 'grave' makes the sentence make no sense.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A woman in childbirth, as long as the womb is open,
whether she said: 'I need it,'
or whether she did not say: 'I need it,'
we desecrate שבת for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the oil discussion and gives a new rule about the time frame for desecrating שבת for a יולדת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the womb is open, שבת is desecrated for the חיה whether or not she asks.

steps.title: Starting the rule for after the womb has closed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל begins the second stage, after the womb has closed. This passage breaks off in the middle of his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the womb has closed, whether she said...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. שמואל is starting the contrasting case, after the womb has closed, and the rule will be finished in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same 'whether she said / whether she did not say' pattern is coming again. This hints that after the womb closes, what she says will start to matter. The actual ruling continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Once the womb closed, whether she said
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's statement with the opposite stage, after the womb has closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begins the rule for the period after the womb closes. The ruling itself is completed on the next amud.
